Antelope Canyon & Horseshoe Bend

Plan chauffeured transportation to Page around a confirmed Navajo-led Antelope Canyon tour, Horseshoe Bend access, meal timing, and the long return to Scottsdale.

Highlights

  • Upper or Lower Antelope Canyon
  • Horseshoe Bend overlook
  • Lake Powell views
  • Glen Canyon Dam
  • Navajo Nation guided tour
  • Photography subject to operator rules

A typical day

  1. Pickup timed to the confirmed tour check-in
  2. Drive to the confirmed Page check-in location
  3. Antelope Canyon guided tour (Navajo-led)
  4. Lunch in Page
  5. Horseshoe Bend visit using current official access guidance
  6. Glen Canyon Dam viewpoint if timing allows
  7. Return to Scottsdale

Frequently asked questions

Do we need to book Antelope Canyon separately?

Yes. Guests must reserve and pay an authorized Navajo tour operator directly. The chauffeur does not enter Antelope Canyon; transportation ends at the operator's confirmed check-in location. Send that location and time for route review.

How difficult is the Horseshoe Bend hike?

Review the current official trail, weather, and accessibility guidance before the date. Bring water and plan the check-in and return window around current conditions. Horseshoe Bend parking is operated by the City of Page, and its separate parking fee is not covered by National Park Service passes.

Is this trip worth the long drive?

This is a long transportation day, so review the total drive time, required tour check-in, walking conditions, and return window before booking. The final schedule is confirmed in writing.
